page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.metal-24xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by Intel Xeon 8559C processors. It features 96 vCPUs, corresponding to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading, running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix mathematics. The system is equipped with 768 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8 GB of RAM per physical core.

A primary differentiator of this instance is its massive local storage capacity, offering 60,000 GB of NVMe SSD storage. This high-density local storage is coupled with a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. The server does not include any dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on its host CPU architecture for computational tasks.

In benchmark evaluations, the i7ie.metal-24xl demonstrates top-tier performance across several categories. It achieves top 10% placement in Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, and Passmark CPU tests. Database operations and static web serving throughput also rank in the top 10%, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and medium-model LLM prompt processing show exceptional throughput. Single-core performance and large-model text generation fall into the average to strong ranges, indicating that workloads benefit most from highly parallelized execution.

Given its massive local NVMe storage and high-capacity DDR5 memory, this bare-metal server represents a high-resource-density tier. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring extreme local storage capacity and high IOPS without the overhead of network-attached storage. The hardware profile is optimized for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, high-throughput data warehousing, data-intensive analytics, and enterprise-grade software compilation.
